Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme's security team is working through our SIG/CAIQ and needs a short evidence package focused on encryption and key management so we can close the control items. Specifically we need: 

- Confirmation of KMS vs HSM usage (who is the KMS provider, if HSMs are used who is the supplier and where are they managed).
- Confirmation of at-rest encryption algorithms and whether encryption is always-on for customer data.
- In-transit encryption protocols and TLS versions supported.
- Description of key lifecycle and rotation policy (frequency, automated/manual, rotation logs).
- Whether BYOK / customer-managed keys are supported and any limitations.
- A short architecture diagram showing where CMKs and data keys live relative to the platform.
- Redacted audit evidence (rotation logs, KMS access audit) and the SOC 2 page that covers key management.

Target date to get this to our security team is EOD Tuesday (2026-02-17). If you can provide a small zip/Drive link with the artifacts and a one-page summary that would be ideal.

Let me know if you need to loop in someone from your infra/security team.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Security Engineer, Acme Studios

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com

Quick status update and items I'm attaching for review: redwood_kms_architecture_v1.pdf and kms_policy_snippet.txt (policy excerpt). High-level notes below — please review and flag anything for legal/security redaction: 

- Hosted: we use our managed KMS service backed by cloud provider KMSs (multi-cloud: AWS KMS + GCP KMS) with envelope encryption. The service runs under our control plane; DEKs are ephemeral on GPU nodes.
- Dedicated: reserved pools can optionally be configured with customer-managed keys (CMKs) stored in Redwood-managed HSMs or integrated with customer KMS via Customer-provided KMS connectors (BYOK).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): supports BYOK where the customer supplies keys via HSM import or KMS federation; we never export customer CMKs.\n
Cryptography & protocols: AES-256-GCM for data keys at-rest, RSA-3072 for asymmetric wrapping for some onboarding flows. In-transit uses TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred; we support modern cipher suites and HTTP/2 where negotiated.

Rotation & lifecycle (summary):
- Master key rotation cadence: yearly for root/master CMKs (automated where managed by cloud KMS);
- Data key rotation: 90-day rotation for long-lived DEKs where applicable; short-lived DEKs generated per session for inference caches.
- All rotation events are recorded in KMS audit logs with requestor, operation, and key versions.

Attached: architecture PDF and policy snippet. Evelyn — once you drop the rotation CSV I'll redact and combine before packaging. Diego — confirm HSM attestation file and SOC redaction scope.

-Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround window. Attached is the evidence package we discussed (links below). Summary highlights are in the one-page summary inside the Drive folder. Artifacts included (redacted where required):

- redwood_kms_architecture_v1.pdf — diagram showing Hosted/Dedicated/Private key boundaries and envelope encryption flow.
- kms_policy_snippet.txt — excerpt of KMS access policy and key usage controls.
- kms_rotation_logs_q1_2026.csv — redacted rotation events showing key_id, rotation_time, actor(role) and key_version.
- hsm_supplier_attestation_techsonic.pdf — supplier attestation for our HSM vendor (TechSonic).
- soc2_type2_redacted_2025.pdf — SOC 2 Type II report (page excerpt relevant to cryptographic controls, redacted).
- caiq_answers_redwood_2026.xlsx — completed CAIQ section for encryption & key management.

Short clarifications:
- BYOK: Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted customers we offer customer-managed-key integrations in some regions — please let me know if Acme expects BYOK for production data in Hosted and we can discuss options.
- Rotation: master CMKs are rotated annually; DEKs rotate every 90 days by default and we also issue short-lived session keys for inference caching.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (1.3 preferred) across all endpoints; mutual TLS is optional for Private deployments.

Drive link (redacted access): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/redwood-kms-package
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/0/record/ACME-DEAL-4821

If your security team wants a short 30-min tech walkthrough on Monday to run through any of the artifacts, we can schedule with Rishi and Diego.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
